proposals.spec_says: free the extent on SSD (if in BlockDevice state)
proposals.code_does: remove also frees the extent of a MemoryTier entry whose write-through has landed (flip, second lookup, remove_extent via drive_index); its lookups release a read reference only when they took one

edits.old: - **FR-009**: The `remove(key)` method MUST free the memory-tier slot (if present via `mt.remove()`), free the extent on SSD (if in BlockDevice state), and remove the dispatch map entry.
edits.new: - **FR-009**: The `remove(key)` method MUST free the memory-tier slot (if present via `mt.remove()`), free the extent on SSD (if the entry has one: a BlockDevice entry, or a MemoryTier entry whose write-through has landed and recorded its `ssd_offset`), and remove the dispatch map entry. Its own dispatch-map lookup MUST release only a read reference that lookup acquired: a `NotExist` answer takes none, so none is released. *(Sync 2026-10-23, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-ssd-extent` — code authoritative, commits `a7444f4ab` and `765f75ba3`, repair of root causes #9 and #12. Before it, `LookupResult::MemoryTier` hid the `ssd_offset`, so the extent of a persisted resident entry leaked and the key came back from SSD after a `format_on_init=false` restart (SC-003); and a lookup that answered `NotExist` still released a read reference, which could decrement the write-through pin of a concurrently registered entry.)*

edits.old: A client application wants to evict a cache entry. The client calls the dispatcher's remove method with a cache key. The dispatcher removes the entry from the memory-tier (if present), removes the dispatch map entry, and frees the SSD extent (if the entry was in BlockDevice state).
edits.new: A client application wants to evict a cache entry. The client calls the dispatcher's remove method with a cache key. The dispatcher removes the entry from the memory-tier (if present), removes the dispatch map entry, and frees the SSD extent (if the entry has one: it is in BlockDevice state, or it is memory-tier resident and its write-through has landed).

proposals.spec_says: A `remove` that is refused ... returns `KeyNotFound` and frees nothing. / When it returns `KeyNotFound`, nothing was freed.
proposals.code_does: a refused remove restores a flipped entry with promote_block_to_memory_tier(key, pointer, size): still MemoryTier, same slot, ssd_offset kept, references kept; while remove runs, other callers can see the entry as BlockDevice

edits.old: A `remove` that is refused because a reader or a client `pin` holds the entry, or because the entry stays write-locked past the dispatch-map wait, returns `KeyNotFound` and frees nothing.
edits.new: A `remove` that is refused because a reader or a client `pin` holds the entry, or because the entry stays write-locked past the dispatch-map wait, returns `KeyNotFound`, frees nothing and leaves the entry as it found it: a memory-tier resident entry is still MemoryTier, with the same slot and its `ssd_offset`, and keeps every reference, so a later lookup is served from DRAM. *(Sync 2026-10-23, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-ssd-extent` — code authoritative, commit `765f75ba3`. To learn a resident entry's SSD offset, `remove` briefly flips it to BlockDevice before it tries the removal (FR-009), and restores it with `promote_block_to_memory_tier` if the removal is refused. While `remove` runs, a concurrent caller can therefore see the entry as BlockDevice; a cold lookup in that window takes the concurrent-promotion recovery (FR-051). Known gap, tracked as align task A-12: a concurrent `clear_memory_tier` in that window removes the entry, and the SSD extent is then not freed.)*

edits.old: - `remove()` guarantees, when it returns `Ok`, that the dispatch map entry is removed, so no new lookup can obtain its memory-tier pointer. When it returns `KeyNotFound`, nothing was freed.
edits.new: - `remove()` guarantees, when it returns `Ok`, that the dispatch map entry is removed, so no new lookup can obtain its memory-tier pointer. When it returns `KeyNotFound` because the entry is held, nothing was freed and the entry is unchanged: same location, same slot, same references (001 edge case "remove").
